items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014

ctx.x: Yeah. That was the time, yeah.

So I think when we came it was us and Wynton and Branford and Roy Hargrove came a little behind us, but we were some of the first, our first recording was album, CD and cassette. So now all that’s changed. But I don’t think the industry saw a lot of things coming. So now with the computer and the digital downloads and then one of the first things that hurt them, you know, Tower Records had come in, like in what was that in the late 70s, early 80s. And they killed all the Mom and Pop stores because they were such…
